newsitem.title: USA: HFS completes review of Avis in bias case.
newsitem.headline: HFS completes review of Avis in bias case.

text.p: HFS Inc said Friday it received the preliminary results of the review by Skadden, Arps, Slate, Meagher & Flom LLP about the procedures and practices in place at Avis Inc for addressing customer complaints of unlawful actions at Avis locations.
HFS commissioned the review late last month after the company was made aware of allegations of racial discrimination against New Hanover Rent-A-Car, a North Carolina Avis franchisee.

HFS announced previously that Avis had begun legal action to terminate the franchise of New Hanover Rent-A-Car, and that it had requested a preliminary injunction against the continued operation of the Avis franchise by New Hanover, pending the outcome of this case.

The review found that in 1992 Avis's Director of Franchising notified the then Avis General Counsel that a number of complaints had been received alleging unlawful discrimination by New Hanover. He requested that New Hanover be notified that discrimination of the sort complained of is illegal and in violation of its franchise agreement.

Avis referred one of these complaints to the attention of the Avis Licensee Association, which reported that New Hanover denied any unlawful discriminatory actions. The then General Counsel took no further action.
The General Counsel concerned is retiring for unrelated reasons and his direct supervisor had retired previously.
Avis recently named a new executive vice president and general counsel, John Carley, effective January 1, who is currently New York State's Deputy Attorney general for Public Advocacy.

The Skadden report contains several recommendations, which Avis will implement, to assure that an appropriate and prompt response is made to any future complaints of unlawful discrimination, including the creation of a specific complaint form for potential discrimination claims. A committee has been formed and will review monthly, any complaints involving allegations of unlawful conduct of any kind, and take all appropriate actions going forward. Carley will chair this committee.

Henry Silverman, HFS chairman and CEO said, "We believe that the potential damage to Avis and its reputation should have been recognized earlier and that more rigorous action should have been taken to attempt to prevent harm to the company and to preserve customer relations. Unfortunately, this was a case of judgment which, in retrospect, was not correct. The express policy of Avis and its employees is that they do not tolerate racism. We have taken steps to ensure that this type of situation does not occur again. We will not tolerate unlawful discriminatory practices of any kind and deeply regret if any customer was subjected to it."
